description: This figure is a single, unlabelled SEM micrograph (no panel letters, no (a)/(b) markers) showing a nano-indentation array on a duplex low-density steel; a scale bar printed "2 µm" sits in the lower-left corner. The field of view is a few tens of micrometres across and contains several microstructural constituents: a flat grey matrix grain occupying most of the centre and left, a roughly vertical band of dark, elongated and blocky precipitates (stringer-like) cutting through the middle, and a second decorated band across the upper-right where bright needle- and plate-shaped particles are set in a darker phase; faint parallel polishing scratches appear at the upper-left and isolated bright spots are scattered throughout. The nano-indentation imprints appear as small dark triangular/pointed marks arranged in regular horizontal rows and roughly a dozen evenly spaced columns, so that rows traverse regions of different grey contrast and therefore different phases. The image supplies the experimental layout used to determine nano-hardness of the individual phases and of phase combinations; no numerical data, axes or legend beyond the 2 µm scale bar are printed on the figure itself.

subfigures.description: Backscattered/secondary-electron SEM micrograph with a 2 µm scale bar in the lower-left corner, showing rows of dark triangular nano-indentation imprints placed across a multiphase microstructure: a featureless grey matrix grain, a roughly vertical dark stringer band of elongated/blocky precipitates, and an upper-right band containing bright needle/plate-shaped particles in a darker phase. Faint polishing scratches at upper-left. No axis labels, values or legends.

observations.observation: The figure is a single SEM micrograph with a printed scale bar of 2 µm in the lower-left corner; no panel letters are present.
Nano-indentation imprints appear as small dark, triangular/pointed marks arranged in regular horizontal rows and evenly spaced vertical columns across the field.

The indentation rows cross regions of different grey contrast (a darker left grain and a lighter central/right area), i.e. the array is deliberately placed over more than one microstructural constituent.

A roughly vertical band of dark, elongated and blocky precipitates (stringer-like) runs through the centre of the image, and a second band containing bright needle/plate-shaped particles occurs at the upper right.
Faint parallel polishing scratches are visible in the upper-left and isolated bright spots (possible residuals/pores) are scattered over the surface.
No numeric hardness values, axes, or legend are printed anywhere on the micrograph; the only annotation is the 2 µm scale bar.
The caption states that the image shows rows of nano-indentations carried out to determine the nano-hardness of different phases present in the microstructure.
Nano-indentation was performed at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 µN s^-1 up to a maximum load of 10000 µN with a hold time of 20 s.
Each phase measurement was repeated at least 25 times, in arrays of 50-70 indentations applied across the region of interest.
The phases individually probed were solution-treated γ and α phases, B2 stringer bands, and both micro-meter sized and nano-disk B2.
Combined hardness values were also determined for γ + cuboid κ, γ + cuboid κ + microsized B2, γ + microsized B2, α + needle-shape κ, and α + nano-disk B2.
The citing text states that the SEM-recorded indent arrays are given as an example (Fig. 3), i.e. the figure is illustrative of the indentation layout rather than of measured hardness values.

measured_quantities: nano-hardness of individual phases and phase combinations (caption; value not printed on the image)
unreadable_items: No panel letters or per-region labels on the micrograph: which indent row corresponds to which named phase/phase combination cannot be determined from the image alone
The exact number of indentation columns/rows is not printed and can only be counted approximately
Composition of the bright needle/plate-shaped particles and of the dark stringer precipitates is not labelled in the image (only inferable from the citing text)
